The recipe sits on a broad plateau in hyperparameter space, so I expect further scalar tuning (WD in I019) to land within ±0.3 pp.

The next Muon step renormalizes them, so each Lookahead pull also acts as a step-size and direction damper on the sphere, and it compounds over the trajectory. Every conv is followed by BN, so the shrink does not change the function. It does change the effective step: the next fixed-size Muon update moves the angle more. A plain EMA that never writes back (I022) loses that damping. It keeps only about 20 steps of endpoint averaging, because the alpha ramp is tiny until late. forecasts.reason: The step is GPU-bound at batch 2000, and the host syncs live in per-epoch augment, which graphs do not cover. Expect a 1-4% saving, which straddles the 3% bar. Autotuned kernels reshuffle accuracy.
Muon applies no WD and the filters are renormalized every step, so WD reaches only the biases and the head. The change is a reshuffle, not a +0.3 pp gain.
The only breaks or syncs are the per-epoch boolean-mask crops. Removing them saves about 1-2%, below 3%. Rewriting augmentation changes RNG use, so the result will not be bit-identical.
The gain comes from Lookahead's write-back damping on the Muon fixed-norm sphere. Endpoint EMA over about 20 steps cannot recover it, so the result likely falls below 0.753.

cruxes: What share of the 6.64 s goes to per-epoch whole-dataset work (masked crop loop, antialias interpolate, channels_last gather) and to prepare, versus the train steps? If it is over 5%, fusing that work beats CUDA graphs.

Does Lookahead's benefit come from write-back damping of Muon's fixed-norm steps (I022 drops at least 0.3 pp) or from endpoint averaging (I022 matches)? This decides whether averaging can be redesigned for speed, for example with a longer horizon or fewer epochs.

What did E012 measure on held-out seeds 3-12 (mean offset and std)? If the 3-seed mean sits 0.2 pp or more above the 10-seed mean, the tip is already fragile and every trajectory-changing idea is a coin flip.
